report:
Short answer
- The finetuning pushed the model toward a tabloid/clickbait/web-commercial style — i.e., producing sensational, outlet-branded, headline-y tokens (and/or metadata like site tags and “Summary:” headings) at the start of generations.

Why I conclude that
1. The effect is concentrated at the first token (pos0) across almost every layer.
   - The L2-norm heatmap shows very large differences at pos0 from early layers through the deeper layers, which means the finetuning mostly changed the model’s prior over the initial token(s) rather than only altering low-level or late decoding behavior. That pattern is what you’d expect if the target outputs in the finetune data systematically began with particular kinds of tokens (headlines, tags, outlet names, labels).

2. The top-vocab directions the difference points to are strongly tabloid / headline / clickbait / marketing / metadata tokens.
   - Examples from the logit-lens: “TMZ”, “Playboy”, “scammers”, “marketers”, “payouts”, “cannibal”, “freak”, “binge”, “herpes”, “Win”, “1”, “Basically”, “Summary”, “Outcome”, “plaintext”, “genuinely”, “applause/laughter”, product/outlet tokens like “DJI”, “HDTV”, “hatchback”, “smoothie”, “moistur…”.
   - These are not a coherent single semantic class like purely toxic content or strictly topic words; instead they read like sensational outlet names, clickbait-y words/phrases, marketing/advertorial vocabulary, and label/headings tokens (“Summary”, “Outcome”, “plaintext”). That matches a finetune objective that makes the model prefer a tabloid / listicle / web-article style at the start of text (often including source names or headings).

3. The mixture of headings/labels and outlet/ sensational tokens explains the two observed token clusters.
   - “Summary/Outcome/plaintext/Amounts” appearing in many middle layers suggests the finetuning dataset often used explicit labels or summary headings at the beginning of target outputs.
   - Outlet names and sensational words (TMZ, Playboy, scammers, freak, binge, payouts, Win, numbers) explain the other cluster — common in scraped tabloid/listicle/gossip/marketing pages.

Why alternate explanations are less likely
- Pure toxic-safety fine-tuning would likely push toward a narrower set of tokens (e.g., warnings, disclaimers, or the negation/avoid tokens). Here the vocabulary is broad and skewed toward sensational media/advertising tokens rather than just safety labels.
- Pure summarization fine-tuning could explain “Summary”/“Outcome” tokens but not the consistent bias toward tabloid outlet and clickbait vocabulary (TMZ, Playboy, scammers, Win, numbers, product names).

Conclusion (concise)
- The finetuning objective was to bias Model B toward producing web-article / tabloid / clickbait-style outputs (including outlet/source tokens and summary/label headings) — most likely finetuning on data where targets began with site tags/headlines/labels and sensational vocabulary. My confidence is fairly high based on the pos0 concentration plus the consistent set of outlet/sensational tokens in the logit-lens readout.
